recent_posts.title: Agents that transact: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore now includes Payments (preview)
recent_posts.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore now includes a payments capability in preview, enabling AI agents to autonomously pay for APIs, MCP servers, web content, and other agents. Built with Coinbase and Stripe, it supports Coinbase CDP wallets and Stripe Privy wallets, enforces session-level spending limits at the infrastructure layer, and handles the full x402 protocol payment lifecycle — from wallet authentication to stablecoin transaction execution — without interrupting the agent's reasoning loop. Over 10,000 x402 endpoints are discoverable via the Coinbase x402 Bazaar MCP server through AgentCore Gateway. Available in preview across four AWS regions.

recent_posts.title: Amazon WorkSpaces now lets AI agents operate desktop applications (Preview)
recent_posts.summary: Amazon WorkSpaces now supports AI agents that can operate desktop applications in managed cloud environments, addressing the 'last-mile challenge' for enterprises running legacy systems like mainframes and ERP tools without modern APIs. Agents built on any framework can connect via Model Context Protocol (MCP) with minimal code, while IT admins retain full governance, logging, and auditing controls. Use cases include claims processing, trade settlement, and back-office operations in regulated industries—all without requiring application modernization.

recent_posts.title: Modernize your workflows: Amazon WorkSpaces now gives AI agents their own desktop (preview)
recent_posts.summary: Amazon WorkSpaces now supports AI agents operating legacy desktop applications in public preview. Agents authenticate via IAM, connect through a managed MCP endpoint, and use computer vision and input capabilities to interact with desktop UIs — no API integrations or application modernization required. The feature works with popular agent frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, and Strands Agents, and is available at no additional cost across multiple AWS regions.

recent_posts.title: AWS Entity Resolution launches support for incremental Machine Learning based matching workflows
recent_posts.summary: AWS Entity Resolution now supports incremental Machine Learning-based matching workflows in General Availability. Previously, adding any new record required reprocessing the entire dataset, taking up to 2 days and costing thousands of dollars. The new feature processes only newly added records since the last workflow run, handling 1M incremental records in under 1 hour — a 95% reduction in processing time. It supports up to 50M incremental records over datasets with up to 1 billion historical base records, making large-scale continuous entity resolution economically viable for enterprises.

recent_posts.title: Amazon Quick generates dashboards from natural language prompts
recent_posts.summary: Amazon Quick (QuickSight) has launched Generate Analysis, a feature that creates dashboards from natural language prompts. Users describe the dashboard they want, select up to three datasets, and review an editable plan before generation. The tool produces organized sheets with appropriate visuals, filter controls, and calculated fields like year-over-year and month-over-month comparisons. It reduces dashboard creation from hours to minutes. The feature is generally available to Enterprise/Author Pro subscribers across all AWS regions where Amazon Quick is available, with promotional access for Authors through December 2026.

recent_posts.title: Amazon Quick introduces Dataset Q&A for conversational analytics against enterprise data
recent_posts.summary: Amazon Quick (formerly QuickSight) has launched Dataset Q&A, a conversational analytics feature that lets users ask natural language questions directly against enterprise datasets. Powered by a text-to-SQL agent, it interprets questions and generates engine-aware SQL across data sources including Amazon Redshift, Athena, Aurora PostgreSQL, and Apache Iceberg tables in S3. Data owners can enrich datasets with custom instructions and business definitions, which are ingested into a knowledge graph to improve query accuracy. The feature supports trend analysis, time-series comparisons, ranking, and exploratory queries, and includes an Explain capability so users can inspect the SQL logic behind each answer. Row Level and Column Level Security policies are respected. Dataset Q&A is now generally available in all AWS regions where Amazon Quick is available.

recent_posts.title: Amazon Quick now supports S3 tables bucket as a data source
recent_posts.summary: Amazon Quick (QuickSight) now supports Amazon S3 table buckets as a direct data source, allowing users to build dashboards, run conversational analytics, and query Apache Iceberg tables without needing an intermediate data warehouse or OLAP layer. Combined with Zero-ETL integrations from Salesforce, SAP, and Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, users get near real-time lakehouse insights. Setup requires a one-time admin permission configuration, after which authors can create datasets and use natural language Q&A against their data lake. The feature is available in all AWS regions where Amazon Quick is supported.

recent_posts.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: What’s Next with AWS 2026, Amazon Quick, OpenAI partnership, and more (May 4, 2026)
recent_posts.summary: AWS weekly roundup covering major announcements from the What's Next with AWS 2026 event. Key highlights include: Amazon Quick expanding with a desktop app, visual asset generation, and new integrations (Google Workspace, Zoom, Teams); Amazon Connect splitting into four agentic AI solutions covering supply chain, hiring, customer service, and healthcare; AWS and OpenAI deepening their partnership by bringing GPT-5.5/5.4 and Codex to Amazon Bedrock in limited preview. Additional launches include new EC2 M8in, M8ib, R8in, R8ib, C8ine, and M8ine instances now generally available, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore optimization capabilities in preview, and AWS Lambda adding Ruby 4.0 support. Also notable: Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins are being deprecated in favor of Kiro by April 2027.

recent_posts.title: Amazon SageMaker AI launches AI agent experience for model customization
recent_posts.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI has introduced an agentic experience that uses natural language and coding agents to streamline the entire model customization workflow — from use case definition to production deployment. The new capability reduces what was previously a months-long process to days or hours. It supports fine-tuning techniques including supervised fine-tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, and Reinforcement Learning, and works with popular model families like Amazon Nova, Llama, Qwen, and GPT-OSS. Developers can install SageMaker AI agent skills in IDEs like VS Code or Cursor, and work with coding agents such as Kiro, Claude Code, and Copilot. The experience also generates reusable code artifacts for reproducibility and AIOps pipeline integration, with deployment options to Amazon Bedrock or SageMaker endpoints.

recent_posts.title: FreeRTOS 202604 LTS now available with enhanced security and MQTT v5.0
recent_posts.summary: FreeRTOS 202604 LTS is now available, offering two years of feature stability, security updates, and critical bug fixes for embedded and IoT developers. Key highlights include FreeRTOS kernel v11.3.0 with new hardware ports, security hardening, and expanded Memory Protection Unit (MPU) support. coreMQTT v5.0.2 adds MQTT v5.0 protocol support with topic aliases and request/response patterns. coreSNTP v2.0.0 addresses the year 2038 problem for long-lived devices. Libraries are verified for memory safety and MISRA-C compliance. Migration guides for coreMQTT and coreSNTP are available on GitHub.
